name: Nubank
thesis: Digital-native bank scaling across LatAm with structurally lower cost-to-serve. Brazil is maturing into a deepening cross-sell story; Mexico (banking license underway) and Colombia are the next-leg compounders. The compounder is per-customer monetization (ARPAC + cross-sell) × ex-Brazil customer expansion.
key_driver: Mexico + Colombia customer scale-up combined with cross-sell monetization deepening

tier_1_kpis.note: Q1-Q3'25 disclosure basis; track for continuity

tier_1_kpis.name: ARPAC/CTS ratio
tier_1_kpis.note: Replaces simple cost-to-serve QoQ trigger; captures unit-economics direction

break_conditions: ARPAC declining QoQ for 2 consecutive quarters
NPL 90+ Brazil consumer > 8% (Q1-Q3'25 basis) OR NPL 90+ Group > 6% (Q4'25 onward basis)
ARPAC/CTS ratio falling for 2 consecutive quarters
schema_revision_notes: 2026-05-04: Bifurcated NPL 90+ into Brazil-consumer and Group buckets to handle the Q4'25 methodology consolidation (geography mix). Re-baselined Revenue threshold from <25% to <20% (the $5B/Q base makes 25% mechanically unreachable in 2026). Replaced mechanically-safe customer net-adds 2M floor with Mexico growth (the leading indicator now that Brazil is saturated at 62% adult-pop). Replaced cost-to-serve QoQ trigger with ARPAC/CTS ratio direction.

nuance.bear_case: Brazil customer count saturating at 113M (62% adult pop) means future BR growth depends entirely on monetization — and BR macro (Selic elevated, credit cycle turning) could compress NPL buffer. Regional ARPAC opacity makes it hard to verify whether MX/CO cohorts are tracking toward BR-level monetization.
nuance.adversarial_take: Mexico banking license has been 'underway' for multiple quarters — execution risk if regulatory approval drags into 2027. Cost-to-serve at $0.80 is at a scale floor; further leverage requires automation gains, not just volume.
nuance.stress_test: NPL 90d+ at 6.6% is only 40bps from the 7% break threshold. A Brazil credit cycle turn flips this metric first; combined with any deceleration in MX/CO net adds, the thesis re-rates quickly.

thesis_breakers_qualitative: Mexico banking license rejected or delayed beyond mid-2027
BR macro deterioration spiking NPL above 7%
Ecosystem cross-sell stalling (% of base flat for 2+ Qs)
Regional ARPAC (when disclosed annually in 20-F) showing MX/CO at <30% of BR ARPAC for 2+ years
open_disclosure_asks: Quarterly ARPAC by region (BR / MX / CO) — currently only annual / inconsistent
Cross-product attach rate (avg products per active customer) by region — derivable from 20-F but not quarterly
